messages.snippet: JITC Digest – June 2026 In This Issue: Letter from the Editor | JITC Editor Picks SITC 40 th Anniversary Special Series | Popular Articles Letter from the Editor Hello JITC Readers, June is Cancer
messages.body:
JITC Digest Header


JITC Digest – June 2026

In This Issue: Letter from the Editor | JITC Editor Picks 
SITC 40th Anniversary Special Series | Popular Articles

LETTER FROM THE EDITOR

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Hello JITC Readers,



June is Cancer Immunotherapy Month—a time to celebrate the remarkable progress
our field has achieved and recommit ourselves to the work that remains. As we
celebrate this month, I am delighted to shareJITC’snew 2025 Impact Factor of
11.7—an outstanding achievement that shows the continued strength, influence,
and growth of our journal, and placesJITCamong the top 5% of all immunology
journals and the top 9% of all oncology journals. It also serves as a reminder
of the critical role that rigorous, high-quality scientific publishing plays in
advancing cancer research and patient care. As we reflect on the advances that
have transformed cancer care and anticipate the next generation of scientific
breakthroughs, I am reminded of the strength of our global immunotherapy
community and our shared commitment to improving patient outcomes.



Earlier this month at the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual
Meeting, I joined JITC Clinical Cancer Immunotherapy Section Editor Paolo
Antonio Ascierto, MD, to host a “Meet the Editor” session at the SITC exhibit
booth. It was a rewarding opportunity to engage with researchers at every career
stage, discuss the critical role of scientific publishing, and reinforce the
importance of collaboration in advancing cancer immunotherapy.



[https://assets.informz.net/SICIZ/data/images/JITC/Dr.%20Lotze%20ASCO%20MTE.png]

(Left to right – Alanna Kaplan MD, PhD; Elshad Hasanov MD, PhD; Vignesh
Elangovan BS; Michael T. Lotze, MD, FAIO; Karim Vermaelen MD, PhD; and Irina
Krykbaeva MD, PhD. Photo Courtesy of Valerie Ward, SITC). 



ASCO also provided valuable scientific insights and educational opportunities
that continue to shape the future of our field. In the “ASCO Highlights” section
below, I share SITC’s key takeaways from this year’s meeting, along with related 
JITC articles that further explore emerging areas of discovery.



June Article Spotlight – Commentaries, Editorials, and Hypotheses
In recognition of Cancer Immunotherapy Month, we are spotlighting the JITC 
Commentary and Editorials Section, led by Section Editor Christian Capitini, MD.
This section provides expert perspectives on significant developments in the
field, addresses critical challenges, and fosters discussion around emerging
concepts and innovative hypotheses. This month’s featured commentaries place
recent research findings in the broader context of cancer immunobiology, helping
readers better understand their scientific and clinical significance. I
encourage you to explore these articles, along with the many outstanding papers
published in JITC this month, and to consider them as valuable resources for
your own research and scholarship.



In addition to these select commentaries published this past month, don’t miss
an outstanding collection of recent commentaries commemorating SITC’s 40th
Anniversary: I-O Progress and Potential
[https://www.sitcancer.org/blogs/jitc-publications/2025/05/02/sitc-40th-anniversary-i-o-progress-and-potential]
. Luminaries in immuno-oncology provided their insights into current
achievements in various areas of the field while also sharing their personal,
forward-looking vision of where the field is moving in the upcoming decades.



Regards,

pedro-romero%281%29%281%29_26717.jpg [https://maassets.higherlogic.com/image/SITC/Dr._Lotze_JITC_Digest_2841520.png]
Michael T. Lotze, MD, FAIO
Editor-in-Chief
Journal for ImmunoTherapy of Cancer

messages.subject: Resources to guard against elder abuse
messages.snippet: For more information, please visit Schwabsafe. view on web Elder Abuse Awareness Day: A commitment to protecting our seniors. June 15 is Elder Abuse Awareness Day, which is held every year to raise
messages.body:
Charles Schwab & Co., Inc.
 
 









 


 









 
 

 
 



 




 
 

 
https://click.email.schwab.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AAcAAAAAAsmwu7OWFMn3IAlHi1MSjCQDxlog0YhU3R8DXDh4scAqnjiwuLXlCadIrBxaxAkLV4iGoR-bUDSMold9BrEPFIkfO-g_FG5rGcs 
view on web 





 
 





 
 


 
 Elder Abuse Awareness Day: A commitment to protecting our seniors.



 June 15 is Elder Abuse Awareness Day, which is held every year to raise awareness about the challenges older adults face and the importance of protecting them. At Schwab, we’re committed to helping safeguard seniors from financial exploitation and scams. Here are some tips and resources to help you stay connected, strengthen support networks, and reduce vulnerability to fraudsters.


 Here’s how you can help seniors.
 - Stay informed: Keep an open dialogue with older family members about their finances and watch for warning signs like sudden account changes, unusual withdrawals, or confusion about recent transactions. Use our 
https://click.email.schwab.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AAcAAAAAAsmwu7OXOrwdZYOFTWCRD1PxeJTWmGWiX_fZj4_AsaYqzFfahUjgYnLmoLOHG8BBrMSWFvJGmdID3rzS0I2-7JwjzI0nh4OSodE 
Financial Exploitation Prevention Checklist to get the conversation started.
 - Promote account security: Encourage recommended security settings and mobile notifications (like 2-step verification, security alerts, or mobile-approve) and review social media privacy settings to limit what others can see. Learn how at 
https://click.email.schwab.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AAcAAAAAAsmwu7OYEcRDPEkoYGHH7EOyPIE0tjx3z8Wf_1d7o4EY09vtVj1r6F58LUhq_yzeVcv0c7cj8Un19P8updTk7-jRWaUIDMzgQX8 
SchwabSafe (R).
 - Report suspicions: If you suspect financial exploitation, report it to local adult protective services, law enforcement, Schwab, and any other financial institutions.


 Here’s how seniors can protect themselves.
 - Review finances: Regularly monitor accounts for unauthorized activities, and if needed, consider adding someone to your account who can help you manage your money and assets. Check out 
https://click.email.schwab.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AAcAAAAAAsmwu7OZEUr6hLi5YJ74j3nH5EBy9b2v5rLzFpFwobR-26_2FZlPJHaN0l2LUpweAfgUnFiHZUjI6H56PJdLK5LdFvh9gFwlXsc 
Your Guide To Choosing a Financial Caregiver to learn more about formal and informal caregiving.
 - Plan ahead: Keep important financial and legal documents organized and add a trusted contact for another layer of protection. Learn how at 
https://click.email.schwab.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AAcAAAAAAsmwu7OaKn674wM-82KTAn7BczglhgTuexSOS9LNPOu8X0CtPGux0_OWIY_GGzmRAqWkLD363aWCZV75SFvFxizUvHRyMJ2Kb34 
Prepare for the Challenges of Aging and 
https://click.email.schwab.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AAcAAAAAAsmwu7ObmL8u-Uito30Tu9BqZeYwlOKvCvOZ5cfjSLu6vgf8IINO7tEwxeYmNMFAKK1vF51n6NozDlA1SQow5US5Pz45NDYOQXU 
Why You Should Establish Trusted Contacts.
 
 
 
 - Shield personal information: Don’t share account numbers, passwords, or one-time verification codes in response to unexpected calls, texts, emails, or pop-ups. Check out 
https://click.email.schwab.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AAcAAAAAAsmwu7OcZqT4NLdMQf7MWxFLpt88Ln8JXcg3oBDOB0tJCENQfcxp0CXG4FQ2V6NZzhO28w-RzC71rBJkc1HVzAyCIJOUkrvmS5o 
10 Tips for Keeping your Accounts Secure to learn more.
 - Don’t grant unsolicited remote access. Avoid clicking on unknown links or granting device access unless you initiated the conversation and can verify who you’re dealing with—fraudsters can use it to steal information and money.



 Additional resources can be found at 
https://click.email.schwab.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AAcAAAAAAsmwu7OdW93SemXRJhcNr6A-Qh3jLp2Js-ZdiVV7pF6OiRwNRSGDaRcNp3J7OHWGg3Fcd6gG7uAr_TDpsJhJcYr2AIxFQdsQkxo 
Protecting Senior and Vulnerable Investors.

We’re here to help.

Biomedical science moves fast, but the coverage doesn’t always make it easy to see what actually matters. 


I’m excited to announce that we’ll be launching Science Snapshot: a new short-form video series from Harvard Medical School that breaks down some of the most interesting biomedical headlines into clear, concise takeaways. These videos are designed to fit into your day in just a few minutes, and will help you go below the surface level to understand what happened and why it matters.


You’ll see new Science Snapshot videos in upcoming Trends in Medicine newsletter issues and on the 
https://click.mc.oee.hms.harvard.edu/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AA0AAAAAAHpzV1afZJC1FOLF7DFMuHkOhqljaQ6gYFeOBbLVlX2U6FXNGfRz70hjr27eSSVXTAYp2uypUb4AcWEzfD0z1i_Y6DHHU9C2UIaOXKcNHw 
Insights page of our website. Each video will also point you to relevant courses that will help you dive deeper into a subject. 


We hope you’ll watch and learn with us!


Laura Dedmon

Harvard Medical School

Health care is entering an unprecedented period of rapid, technology-enabled transformation. The question now for health care leaders is: what capabilities do they need to spearhead a system that is changing this quickly?


“If you’re not getting up to speed on AI right now, you’re already behind,” explains William Gordon, MD, MBI, staff physician at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and faculty co-director of the new

Dear Julia,

We sincerely apologize for the long wait.

Your order has now completed production and passed quality inspection. It is currently scheduled for departure on June 11th, with an estimated arrival at the destination port around June 28th.

After arrival, it will take approximately 1 week for customs clearance, unloading, and transportation to our overseas warehouse, after which the final delivery will be arranged.

We truly appreciate your patience and will keep you updated as your order progresses.

Warm regards,
Mabel

messages.subject: Your New Social Security Statement is now available
messages.snippet: Dear Julia: Your Social Security Statement is streamlined and easier to read than ever before. That is because we have redesigned the Statement to provide you the most useful information up front and
messages.body:
Dear Julia:

Your Social Security Statement is streamlined and easier to read than ever before. That is because we have redesigned the Statement to provide you the most useful information up front and at a glance.

We encourage you to check your Statement at least once a year to review:
-Your earnings record (to make sure it's accurate and notify us if you see any errors);
-Your personalized monthly retirement benefit estimates (which now display how much you can expect to receive depending on when you decide to start your benefits between ages 62 and 70); 
-Other useful information that will explain your benefits and help you prepare for your financial future; and
-New fact sheets that provide additional information based on your specific age group and earnings situation.

You can access your new Statement by signing into your account at socialsecurity.gov/reviewyourstatement. 

Now that you can access your Statement instantly and anytime online, we will not automatically send one by mail.

We hope you find your new Statement useful and informative.

https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f5b&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548
We're just getting started! Day two of the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f5c&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548 begins at 8 AM (CT) today. You'll want to catch the Opening Session https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f5d&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548 at 9:45 AM (CT), featuring Dr. Eric Small's Presidential Address on The Science and Practice of Translation: Improving Cancer Outcomes Worldwide. Poster sessions and the Exhibit Hall open today at 9 AM (CT) in Hall A. Other can't-miss sessions include:
​
Special Clinical Science Symposium: ctDNA in Clinical Practice: From Early Detection to Clinical Decision-Making https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f5e&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548 8 AM (CT) in Hall D1 and Livestream
ASCO/AACR Joint Session: The KRAS Journey—Perseverance Pays Off https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f5f&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548 1:15 PM (CT) in Room S100bc and Livestream
The Best of JCO Global Oncology: Improving Affordability in Cancer Care for Resource-Limited Settings https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f60&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548 (Limited Attendance; First-Come, First-Served) at 4:45 PM (CT) in S403
Oral Abstract Sessions in Breast Cancer; Central Nervous System Tumors; Genitourinary Cancer; Hematologic Malignancies; and Sarcoma
Rapid Oral Sessions in Care Delivery and Quality Care; Developmental Therapeutics; Gynecologic Cancer; Hematologic Malignancies; Lung Cancer; Melanoma/Skin Cancers; and Pediatric Oncology.
​
Late-breaking abstracts (LBAs) presented today will be available online https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f61&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548 7 AM (CT), and posters will be available online beginning at the start time of their scheduled sessions. All session recordings, plus downloadable transcripts and slides, will be available within 24 hours of each session's end time.
Watch Livestream Sessions https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f62&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548
You will need to log in to view or interact with session content. As a reminder, your username is JuliaJoy and the primary email address associated with your account is juliajoyjennings@gmail.com. If you have issues logging in, please contact Customer Service https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f63&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548
Save 25% on ASCO Membership
Join or renew by stopping by ASCO Central to manage your membership. Attending online? Use code: ASCO26MEM25 to receive a 25% discount at checkout https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f64&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548 Take advantage of this exclusive offer through June 5 and expand your professional oncology community. 
Onsite Opportunities

Stop by the Survival Station in ASCO Central for some quick fixes that may help you get through your long day. If you need a break from science, head to the ASCO Garden on the D2 Terrace to relax and enjoy live music on the shore of Lake Michigan or catch the UEFA Champions League final today at 11 AM (CT). You should also check out the Wellness Zone in the South Building S103 lobby for a quiet place to recharge. Complimentary massages are available (first come, first served). 
Important Reminders
Claim your CME credit and request MOC points as you attend sessions using the ASCO Meetings app or the online Program https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f65&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548 We also encourage you to take a few minutes to provide feedback https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f66&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548 your overall meeting experience. Learn more https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t257852f4,803f5ed,3725f67&cid=DM29502&bid=628642548

Rapid Oral Sessions in Care Delivery and Quality Care; Developmental Therapeutics; Gynecologic Cancer; Hematologic Malignancies; Lung Cancer; Melanoma/Skin Cancers; and Pediatric Oncology.
​
Late-breaking abstracts (LBAs) presented today will be available online https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t2577c653,803f5cf,3725f25&cid=DM29500&bid=628606547 7 AM (CT), and posters will be available online beginning at the start time of their scheduled sessions. All session recordings, plus downloadable transcripts and slides, will be available within 24 hours of each session's end time.
Watch Livestream Sessions https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t2577c653,803f5cf,3725f26&cid=DM29500&bid=628606547
You will need to log in to view or interact with session content. As a reminder, your username is JuliaJoy and the primary email address associated with your account is juliajoyjennings@gmail.com. If you have issues logging in, please contact Customer Service https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t2577c653,803f5cf,3725f27&cid=DM29500&bid=628606547
Save 25% on ASCO Membership
Join or renew by stopping by ASCO Central to manage your membership. Attending online? Use code: ASCO26MEM25 to receive a 25% discount at checkout https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t2577c653,803f5cf,3725f28&cid=DM29500&bid=628606547 Take advantage of this exclusive offer through June 5 and expand your professional oncology community. 
Onsite Opportunities

Stop by the Survival Station in ASCO Central for some quick fixes that may help you get through your long day. If you need a break from science, head to the ASCO Garden on the D2 Terrace to relax and enjoy live music on the shore of Lake Michigan or catch the UEFA Champions League final today at 11 AM (CT). You should also check out the Wellness Zone in the South Building S103 lobby for a quiet place to recharge. Complimentary massages are available (first come, first served). 
Important Reminders
Claim your CME credit and request MOC points as you attend sessions using the ASCO Meetings app or the online Program https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t2577c653,803f5cf,3725f29&cid=DM29500&bid=628606547 We also encourage you to take a few minutes to provide feedback https://t4.email.asco.org/r/?id=t2577c653,803f5cf,3725f2a&cid=DM29500&bid=628606547 your overall meeting experience. messages.snippet: 🎉 Your meds have arrived! Hi Julia, your medication has been delivered! Here's what to do next: 1. Check your correct dosage based on the concentration of the vial. Your prescribed units may have
messages.body:
🎉 Your meds have arrived!


Hi Julia, your medication has been delivered! Here's what to do next:


1. Check your correct dosage based on the concentration of the vial. Your 
prescribed units may have gone up or down.


2. Refrigerate your medication once you get it. Do not freeze it!


3. Your vial can provide up to 5 doses if you take your medication on the same 
day each week and have medication remaining (you'll need to discard your vial 
28 days after it's been punctured).


4. Review the instruction video <noom://noom.com/open?open=YOUR_PRESCRIPTIONS> 
about how to take the medication.


5. Learn more about your medication in the Noom app 
<https://dl.noom.com/?email=juliajoyjennings@gmail.com>.

See more tips <https://dl.noom.com/?email=juliajoyjennings@gmail.com>
See more tips <https://dl.noom.com/?email=juliajoyjennings@gmail.com>

If you have any questions, please reach out to your Care Coordinators via 
in-app <https://noomcoach.app.link?open=CHAT_CHANNELS> messaging.




Yours in health, 

The Noom Med Team




 



If you have questions, please contact our support team at noommed@noom.com or 
by replying to this email



One Palmer Square, Suite 441, Princeton, NJ 08542
